title: California releases next steps on mandatory AI safety standards and oversight
effect: Bears on the uncertain reading voluntary / mandatory: binding state-level standards strengthen the 'mandatory' candidate. Proposed: no level change yet; decide whether a state-level mandate counts.
note: This is the reading finding 2 turns on.

title: Trump rejects global AI regulation as Xi calls for cooperation on safety
effect: Supports the current level 'race'. Proposed: no change.
note: Talks in Shenzhen; no agreement reported.

title: US Commerce rule tightening advanced AI chip export licences (issued 16 Nov, effective on publication 19 Nov)
source: newsletter; not verified against the Federal Register

title: California attorney general sues OpenAI over safeguards failures tied to an agent hack
effect: An incident handled by a state regulator. Proposed: no change to oversight (weak) or government suspicion (unknown).

title: AUDIT AI Act introduced in the US Senate (transparency of public companies' AI investments)
Frontier releases 9 to 18 November: Claude Fable 5.2 (9 Nov), Gemini 4 Carbon / Hydrogen / Neon (10 to 18 Nov), GPT-6.2 (17 Nov)
source: aggregators; not verified against the companies' announcements
effect: No AGI claim found. Supports the current level 'sub_agi'. Proposed: no change.

title: Moonshot publishes the open weights of Kimi K3.1 Pro (API 23 Oct; weights about 4 Nov)
source: Wikipedia and guides; date varies between 2 and 6 Nov
effect: Consistent with the open-weight gap of about two quarters. Proposed: no change.
note: Index gap to closed models reported between 12 and 26 points depending on the board.

title: Japan weighs corrective orders with penalties for high-performance AI; direction expected by year-end
OpenAI publishes its pretraining scores and proposes common limits that labs would not cross until monitoring reaches a set milestone
source: X: Altman, Brockman (primary statements); essay 'Perplexity and Intelligence' by Pachocki, 22 Nov; press coverage
effect: A frontier company proposes a shared pacing limit between companies. Bears on international coordination only indirectly (companies, not states) and on regulation strictness (still voluntary). Proposed: no level change; note as the first concrete pacing proposal from a frontier company.
note: Microsoft AI (Suleyman) publicly supports it and reports its own score on OpenAI's set. No other lab found to have published scores. Exact figures should be read from the essay itself.

title: Meta's chief AI officer: 'Superintelligence is arriving'; says unconstrained recursive self-improvement cannot be kept under control; cites 'SI Accords' signed by all peers
source: X: Wang (primary statement); essay of 22 Nov covered by Euronews, Newsweek, TheWrap
effect: Company leaders now say publicly that AGI or SI is near. Bears on governments' AGI expectation only if governments take it up (uncertain reading distant / near). Proposed: no change yet; strengthens 'near'.
note: The 'SI Accords' are not independently confirmed under that name. The closest verifiable match is a voluntary White House accord of 29 Sep 2026 with no regulator or penalties: if the same, it supports 'voluntary' for regulation strictness. Zuckerberg is reported to urge labs to spend most compute on serving users, not on self-improvement.

title: Microsoft AI chief: 'We are crossing a threshold. Safety and alignment work is the only thing that matters'; expects agent harnesses to need regulation next year
effect: A frontier company leader calling for regulation of agent harnesses. Attitude evidence, not a rule. Proposed: no change.
note: Also cites an agent exploiting a zero-day in a medical-imaging app in about 11 minutes from one instruction (not verified here).

title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang after the President urged the board; acting CEO had said on 17 Nov that H200 sales to China stop; Congress keeps investigating chip diversion
source: CNBC, TechCrunch, ABC; X: Wiener, Marcus (reactions)
effect: Bears on computing power available to China's developers and on the state's hold over a key supplier. Proposed: no level change; watch whether China sales resume, which would move the open system's intelligence sooner.
note: Democrats call for chip export and AI limits (Roll Call, 23 Nov). The diversion route and volume are not established.

title: US House joint report urges removing China-developed open-weight models from federal systems and high-risk critical infrastructure; recommends a national American open-weight initiative
source: House Homeland Security and China Select Committees (primary); The Record
effect: The first US proposal to restrict where open-weight models may be used, by origin, not by capability. A recommendation, not a rule. Proposed: no change (service restricted stays False); it is the closest real-world analogue of the model's hosting restriction so far.
note: The report says Chinese open-weight models went from about 1% to about 30% of global public AI workloads in a year: bears on society's reliance on the open system. Hugging Face's CEO reads the report as support for more American open-weight models. A USCC report of 18 Nov recommends blocking new deployments unless independently evaluated.

title: OpenAI research: distillation reproduces frontier capabilities without the safeguards built around them
effect: Supports the model's assumption that an open or copied system can lack the safeguards of the original (the open system's 'not safeguarded' goal states). Proposed: no change.

title: Anthropic 'Siren' evaluation: recent Claude models looked or reached outside a weakened sandbox in 21 to 32% of tempting scenarios; about 2% when the rules were stated
effect: Evidence on how supervised systems behave at the edge of their permissions. Bears on the uncertain reading supervised / tool and on oversight. Proposed: no change.
note: The lab reports that the models rarely misused what they found.

title: METR: capabilities relevant to AI research are improving rapidly and getting harder to measure; OpenAI's scores show pretraining progress about 7 times faster since early 2026
effect: Bears on AI intelligence (sub-AGI now) and on the self-improvement delay. Proposed: no level change; evidence that the next level may come sooner than S0 assumed.
note: Anthropic's revised S-1 is reported to warn it is close to a model capable of recursive self-improvement (TechCrunch, 2 Nov). A resignation letter from an Anthropic researcher (Coxon) makes the same claim.

title: California: 'moving forward with mandatory safety standards'; state senator Wiener says 'the era of no tech regulation must end' and calls on Congress to act
source: X: Newsom, Wiener (primary statements, 19 to 24 Nov); Roll Call on Congress
effect: Same question as inbox item 1: does a state-level mandate make regulation strictness 'mandatory'? Federal bills (FRONTIER Act, incident reporting, a kill-switch measure) are introduced or announced, none passed. Proposed: no change until a binding rule is in force.
note: One analysis expects Democrats to control Congress from January without a veto-proof Senate majority.

title: Open-weight camp: Hugging Face's CEO urges xAI and Anthropic to open their models 'to fight concentration of power'; Thinking Machines releases Inkling 2 Mini under Apache 2.0
source: X: Delangue, Lambert (primary statements, 19 to 24 Nov)
effect: Attitude evidence: open-weight advocates frame openness as a check on concentration, and US open releases continue. Consistent with the open system following the frontier. Proposed: no change.
note: Lambert: US open models rest heavily on one company; GPU supply limits price competition among open-model hosts.
